title: Accounts Assistant
description:
As an Accounts Assistant in Warrington, you will handle day-to-day accounting tasks within the retail business, helping to keep financial records accurate and up to date. You will work as part of the Accounting & Finance department and provide reliable administrative support that helps the team run smoothly.

Client Details

The organisation operates in the retail industry in Warrington.

Description

Key Responsibilities
- Processing invoices: Managing and recording supplier and customer invoices.
- Reconciliation: Balancing accounts by reconciling bank statements and financial transactions.
- Data entry: Inputting financial data into accounting systems, ensuring accuracy.
- Expense claims: Processing employee expense claims and ensuring compliance with company policies.
- Credit control: Assisting with managing outstanding payments and debt collection.
- Making daily payments: Processing payments to suppliers and other creditors, ensuring timely and accurate transfers.
- VAT returns: Assisting in preparing VAT returns and other tax documentation.
- Supporting the Head of Finance: Providing administrative and financial support, including helping with audits, financial analysis, budgeting and forecasting tasks.
- Providing administrative support across payroll, HR and office operations, including maintaining records, supporting business processes and assisting with ad hoc projects and administrative activities as directed by the Head of Finance and General Manager.

Profile
- Experience in an accounts assistant or similar finance role.
- Strong numerical skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage workloads and meet deadlines.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and accounting software (e.g., Sage, Xero, QuickBooks).
- Knowledge of accounting principles, financial regulations, credit control and payroll processing.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills with an excellent telephone manner.
- Highly organised with strong multi-tasking skills and ability to work under strict deadlines.
- A proactive, methodical and self-motivated approach to work.
- Accuracy and attention to detail, comfortable working in a busy, fast-paced environment.
- Flexible approach to work, especially during peak periods.
- Willingness to support wider business functions including payroll, HR administration and office operations.
- Ability to build effective working relationships and act as a trusted support to the Head of Finance and wider management team.
- Strong commercial awareness with a confident and determined attitude.
- Ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
- Must be able to commute to Birchwood, Warrington.

Job Offer
- Permanent Accounts Assistant position based in Birchwood.
- Salary of £31,000 to £33,000, dependent on the level of experience.
- Start anytime between 8am and 9am
- 25 days holidays plus BH

title: Credit Control
description:
Credit Controller

Warrington/Hybrid

Salary Circa £30,000

We are looking for an experienced and proactive Credit Controller to join a busy Finance team based in Warrington. This position will play an important role in managing the company's accounts receivable function, ensuring outstanding balances are collected efficiently, maintaining accurate customer accounts and supporting the achievement of monthly cash collection targets.

You will have a strong background in credit control, excellent communication skills and the ability to build effective working relationships with both internal teams and external customers.

Working within a fast-paced and deadline-driven environment, you will need to be highly organised, adaptable and comfortable managing your own workload whilst contributing to wider team objectives.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage the day-to-day credit control process, ensuring customer payments are accurately recorded, posted and allocated.
- Carry out regular customer account reconciliations, investigating and resolving any discrepancies.
- Proactively chase outstanding payments to ensure timely collection of debt and achievement of monthly cash targets.
- Investigate and resolve customer queries and payment disputes, helping to reduce aged debt and minimise potential bad debt exposure.
- Establish and maintain positive relationships with customers and key stakeholders to support effective debt recovery.
- Assess new credit account applications and regularly review existing customer credit limits and risk exposure using external credit reference agencies.
- Maintain accurate customer records and master data within the company's ERP system.
- Produce and distribute monthly debt collection and dunning proposals to relevant stakeholders.
- Oversee the recovery of overdue balances, escalating matters and coordinating legal proceedings where required.
- Work alongside Insolvency Practitioners, preparing relevant documentation and supporting information when necessary.
- Prepare and distribute weekly and monthly aged debtor reports, highlighting collection performance and areas of concern.
- Participate in weekly cash collection meetings, providing updates on outstanding balances, payment risks and key debtor accounts.
- Support the annual audit process by liaising with external auditors and ensuring requested information is provided within agreed deadlines.
- Maintain and update customer portals, ensuring information remains accurate and current.
- Identify opportunities to streamline existing credit control procedures and contribute to ongoing process improvements.
- Provide additional support to the wider Finance team as required.

Skills & Experience Required
- A minimum of 5 years' experience within a Credit Control position, ideally gained in a busy, high-volume finance environment.Experience working towards regular month-end reporting and cash collection targets.
- Strong Excel skills at intermediate to advanced level, including practical experience using Pivot Tables and VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP functions.
- Previous experience working with ERP or accounting systems; knowledge of Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central would be advantageous.
- Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy when handling financial information.

Desirable Qualifications
- Membership of the Chartered Institute of Credit Management (CICM).
- CICM Graduate status or currently studying towards a recognised CICM qualification.
